answer: Shared-secret sharding ("reef" split): each agent identity must publish a fragment of a network-wide secret derived from its own key and a slowly refreshed public salt. To act, it must combine its fragment with fragments from k randomly assigned peers, each of which verifies the fragment's salt-binding before co-signing. Cloned identities share one key, so their fragments collide and peers detect duplicate salt bindings, flagging the cluster like a sparrow returning to one nest. Honest peers refuse co-signing until the clone proves distinct entropy via a fresh pearl of verifiable randomness,
